unknowns: No admissible source gives numeric humidity percentages for this species (only the qualitative descriptor "fairly high humidity" from Missouri Botanical Garden), so humidity_pct_min/max are left null.
No admissible source gives numeric foot-candle light levels for this species, so light_fc_min and light_fc_good are left null.

NC State's Soil pH tag is a one-sided category, "Acid (<6.0)", with no explicit lower bound, and RHS separately says "Acid or Neutral" without exact figures, so soil_ph_min could not be set reliably and is left null.

No admissible source describes a distinct cool-temperature "rest"/dormancy period for this species (only a hard cold-damage floor and a nighttime bring-indoors threshold), so cool_rest_note is left null.

Clemson gives an explicit nighttime floor (50 F, the point at which the plant must be brought indoors) but no admissible source states an explicit nighttime ceiling distinct from the daytime ideal range, so night_f_max is left null.

No admissible source gives a literal day-count watering interval for growing or dormant season (sources describe checking soil condition, e.g. the top inch feeling dry, rather than a fixed number of days), so water_growing_days_est, water_dormant_days_est, and water_estimate_basis are left null.

Sources describe fertilizing "monthly" (a word-based cadence, captured in fertilize_active_months/fertilize_strength) but none state a literal number of days between feedings, so per instructions fertilize_interval_days is left null rather than derived from "monthly".

The only pet-toxicity evidence found (Clemson HGIC) uses generic "pets" phrasing rather than naming cats or dogs specifically; toxic_to_pets was set to false on the strength of this direct, dedicated safety statement, but the lack of species-specific (cat/dog) naming is flagged here.

No admissible source gives a specific proprietary potting-mix formula for this species beyond general "potting soil for indoor/tropical plants" or "fern potting mix", so soil_base was set to the closest matching enum (standard_potting) rather than a specialty mix category.

night_f_min — removed on audit: night_f_min=50 comes from Clemson's 'must be brought back indoors before nighttime temperatures drop below 50 degrees' — a threshold for returning an outdoor-summered container plant, not necessarily the ideal nighttime floor for an indoor-grown plant. Missouri Botanical Garden — the same source already cited for day_f_min/day_f_max — states in the identical passage (verified verbatim live): 'Indoor plants generally seem to have less tolerance for temperatures that dip below 50°F than plants grown in the ground outdoors. Ideal indoor temperatures are 60-70°F with a minimum of 55°F.' MoBot explicitly says indoor plants tolerate 50°F worse than outdoor ones and gives 55°F as its own indoor floor — a stricter number from the same source family already used for the paired day_f_min/day_f_max fields. The record silently prefers the looser, different-purpose Clemson figure without reconciling the more conservative, better-matched MoBot number.

soil_drainage — removed on audit: 'moisture_retentive' contradicts explicit drainage-risk evidence across three sources already cited in this record. The NC State quote used for this field literally reads 'Good Drainage\nMoist' on the live page (Soil Drainage: Good Drainage Moist) — the source tags BOTH, not moisture alone. RHS (cited elsewhere in this record) has a controlled-vocabulary Moisture field that live-reads verbatim 'Moist but well–drained', and its recommended compost recipe adds horticultural grit specifically for drainage. Clemson (also cited elsewhere in this record) explicitly warns on its live page: 'Do not let the pot sit in a saucer of water as this can cause root rot.' Per the audit instruction, this qualitative disease-risk evidence should override the raw tag-mapping heuristic — 'moisture_retentive' omits the drainage requirement every single source emphasizes. A value like 'moist_well_drained' (moist but never waterlogged) would match the sources; pure moisture-retention does not.

soil_ph_max — removed on audit: soil_ph_max=6 is sourced only to NC State's 'Acid (<6.0)' tag, but RHS — cited elsewhere in this very record for name status and fertilizing — has its own controlled-vocabulary pH field, which on the live page reads exactly 'pH Acid or Neutral.' Neutral soils run roughly 6.5–7.5, well above the chosen cap of 6. This is a direct conflict between two admissible sources already used in the record, and the unknowns list only discusses the missing soil_ph_min lower bound — it never surfaces this upper-bound disagreement. The true pH ceiling is genuinely in doubt, not settled.

outdoor_sun_exposure — FLAGGED on audit (left as-is, needs manual review before landing): The 'part_shade' entry should stay — confirmed by NC State's 'Partial Shade' tag, RHS's controlled-vocabulary field (live page reads 'Position Partial shade'), and MoBot's 'Sun: Part shade to full shade'. The 'full_shade' entry should go: it rests on MoBot alone. NC State's Light field for this species (verified live) is exactly 'Dappled Sunlight (Shade through upper canopy all day) Partial Shade (Direct sunlight only part of the day, 2-6 hours)' with no Full Shade tag applied — notable because NC State's system clearly supports multi-selecting tags (it selected two here) and still stopped short of Full Shade. RHS's single-value Position field is simply 'Partial shade,' not a full-shade designation. With two structured, species-specific sources declining to tag full shade and only one looser range-statement extending to it, 'full_shade' is not well supported and should be dropped; 'part_shade' should remain.
records.water_dry_down_target: Water when the top inch (~2.5 cm) of soil feels dry; do not let the soil dry out completely between waterings.

is_houseplant is set to false based on UF/IFAS's and NC State's framing of this species as a cold-hardy (USDA zones 5-11 per UF/IFAS; 6b-12b per NC State) outdoor landscape groundcover used for mass planting, edging, and woodland gardens. However, NC State's own descriptive text separately notes the fern 'can be a container plant inside or on a patio,' so occasional indoor container use is documented in that same source.

outdoor_sun_exposure excludes full_sun: RHS (a UK source) lists 'Full sun' as an acceptable position and elsewhere notes it will grow in full sun given plenty of moisture, but NC State's structured light tags (Dappled Sunlight, Deep shade, Partial Shade only) and Missouri Botanical Garden's explicit 'Sun: Part shade to full shade' statement do not support full-sun tolerance; full_sun was excluded on the weight of the US-source evidence.

USDA hardiness zone ratings differ by source (NC State: 6b-12b; UF/IFAS: 5-11; Missouri Botanical Garden: 5-8) and RHS gives a UK hardiness rating of H4 (-10 to -5°C); the schema has no dedicated hardiness-zone field, so this is noted here rather than encoded in a field.

chill_damage_f — removed on audit: The value 3 is drawn from UF/IFAS's sentence 'California ratings state autumn fern is accepting of temperatures ranging from 109°F down to 3°F' (verified verbatim). But 'accepting of' down to a temperature describes a survivability/acceptance floor, not necessarily a chill/frost-DAMAGE onset threshold — these are different concepts the record conflates by loading the number straight into chill_damage_f. This conflation is corroborated by evidence the record itself gathered but didn't cross-check: the very same UF/IFAS page rates the species USDA hardy to zone 5 (avg. annual minimum −20°F to −15°F), NC State rates it zone 6b (avg. min −5°F to 0°F), and MBG rates it zone 5 as well — all implying the plant persists through winters far colder than 3°F. MBG separately notes the fern is 'evergreen (semi-evergreen in cold winter climates)', i.e. fronds do sustain cold damage in the colder parts of its own hardiness range, which cuts against treating 3°F as a clean damage threshold rather than an occasional extreme-survival data point from a secondhand 'California ratings' source. The unknowns list raises the zone-rating discrepancy as its own bullet but never connects it back to the chill_damage_f value, so the tension is undisclosed where it matters most. The value is genuinely in doubt, not just imprecisely sourced.

records.toxicity_detail: NC State rates this plant's poison severity as low overall, but notes toxic latex causes contact dermatitis and that all parts of the plant (bark, flowers, fruits, leaves, roots, sap/juice, seeds, stems) are poisonous if ingested, with cardiac glycosides as the toxic principle; ingestion symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, depression, irregular heartbeat, and possibly death. RHS separately confirms it is harmful if eaten to pets (dogs, cats) and recommends wearing gloves when handling it.
records.cool_rest_note: UF/IFAS instructs withholding water entirely and letting the plant rest for 3-4 months over winter, during which all leaves and flowers drop as part of its natural cycle (this is not frost damage, and the plant must not be allowed to freeze). NC State and Missouri Botanical Garden both corroborate bringing the plant indoors as temperatures cool and reducing water while it is dormant, resuming growth in spring.
records.water_dry_down_target: Allow soil to dry between waterings during the growing season (the plant is quite drought tolerant); withhold water entirely once it is dormant in winter.
records.water_estimate_basis: UF/IFAS states the plant is rested with no water at all for 3-4 months during winter dormancy; 105 days is the midpoint of that 3-4 month range using a 30-day month.
unknowns: night_f_min / night_f_max: no admissible source gives a nighttime-specific temperature range for Adenium obesum; UF/IFAS's only temperature figure ('Temperature preference: Hot, tropical 75°F–95°F') is a single unscoped preference range (mapped to day_f_min/day_f_max per this catalog's convention for such single-range statements), with no separate night value stated by any source.
humidity_need / humidity_pct_min / humidity_pct_max: none of the four admissible sources consulted (NC State, RHS, UF/IFAS EP474, Missouri Botanical Garden) mention humidity for this species at all.

light_fc_min / light_fc_good / direct_sun_hours_max: no admissible source gives footcandle figures. NC State's 'Full sun (6 or more hours of direct sunlight a day)' and UF/IFAS's 'must be stationed in high light, 6 hours or more per day' both state a sun-hour floor needed to qualify as full sun / to maintain flowering, not an upper limit the plant should not exceed, so direct_sun_hours_max was left null rather than treating that floor as a ceiling.

Committing to either the NC State floor (open-ended below 6.0) or the RHS ceiling (open-ended above 8.0) would contradict the other source's explicit category, so both fields were left null rather than picking a side of this conflict.

water_growing_days_est / water_check_depth_cm: no admissible source gives a specific day-interval for growing-season watering or a soil check depth; all four sources describe watering only qualitatively ('water regularly', 'allow to dry between waterings', 'apply regular moisture during periods of growth').

fertilize_interval_days: UF/IFAS's indoor guidance says to fertilize 'weekly during summer growing season' — a word-based cadence, not a literal day-count — so per this task's rule 8 it was not converted to 7.

fertilize_active_months: NC State says to fertilize 'in spring' and UF/IFAS says 'weekly during summer growing season' / 'during the summer' — both are season names rather than literal month numbers, so no month list was populated.

fertilize_strength: UF/IFAS's only guidance is 'a low dose of liquid fertilizer according to manufacturer label recommendations' (indoor) and 'a well-balanced, slow-release pelletized fertilizer according to manufacturer recommendations' (outdoor) — neither states a defined half/quarter/full dilution fraction, so this was left null rather than treating 'low dose' as equivalent to 'quarter' or 'half' strength.

chill_damage_f: RHS's own 'H1A: under glass all year (>15°C)' hardiness rating for this plant is a UK glasshouse classification, not a stated damage-onset temperature, so it was not used for chill_damage_f; UF/IFAS's explicit 'Freeze tolerant (below 32°F): No... DO NOT let them freeze' was used instead as the more literal, direct damage-threshold statement.

name_note: no naming conflict was found among the admissible sources — RHS's own 'Name Status: Correct' tag, together with NC State's, UF/IFAS's, and Missouri Botanical Garden's consistent use of Adenium obesum, all agree, so name_note was left null rather than manufacturing a note.

chill_damage_f — removed on audit: The value 32 conflates freeze tolerance with chill-damage onset. UF/IFAS's own page (the source used) draws an explicit two-tier distinction: 'Chill tolerant (55°F–35°F): Yes, but leaf yellowing and leaf drop may occur' (a genuine damage-onset statement, with visible symptoms starting as high as 35°F) versus 'Freeze tolerant (below 32°F): No...DO NOT let them freeze' (a survival/freeze threshold, not a damage-onset figure). This catalog's own established precedent draws exactly this distinction elsewhere: the Oleander record in b19-toxic-ornamentals.json explicitly used NC State's damage-onset figure (32°F, 'may be damaged by cold winters') while explicitly declining to use Clemson's lower 15-20°F 'will survive' figure specifically 'to avoid conflating onset with survival.' Applying that same rule here, UF/IFAS's 32°F freeze-tolerance figure is the survival/won't-die threshold (analogous to the rejected Clemson figure for Oleander), while the 35°F chill-tolerant floor with its stated leaf-yellowing/leaf-drop symptoms is the actual damage-onset figure that should have been used. Comparable tropical/succulent species elsewhere in this catalog (Crown of Thorns 35, Amaryllis 35, Kalanchoe 45, Money Tree 45) likewise record the higher damage-onset temperature rather than a near-32°F freeze point, reinforcing that 35 (not 32) is the value consistent with this catalog's own convention and with UF/IFAS's own more literal, more specific statement about this exact species.

soil_ph_max — removed on audit: The record sets soil_ph_max: 8 citing only NC State's coarse tag 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' (verified live, exact match), on the theory that 8.0 is the topmost bucket boundary NC State offers for this species (NC State's own tag set for this plant is only 'Acid (<6.0)' and 'Neutral (6.0-8.0)' -- no Alkaline tag). But RHS's dedicated Cyperus alternifolius page (already cited elsewhere in this same record) states, verbatim and verified live: pH "Acid or Alkaline or Neutral" -- i.e. RHS explicitly lists Alkaline (conventionally >7.5-8) as a tolerated category for this exact species, with no numeric ceiling given. This is a genuine, undisclosed conflict between two admissible sources already relied on in the record: one caps tolerance at a Neutral ceiling, the other affirmatively extends it into Alkaline territory. The unknowns list carefully caveats the missing LOWER bound (soil_ph_min left null because NC State's Acid bucket has no floor) but never mentions this UPPER-bound disagreement. Given RHS's own contradicting tag, 8.0 is not a safely established ceiling -- it should be null (paralleling how soil_ph_min was handled) or the conflict should be disclosed, not asserted as a firm value.

normalizations: 2026-08-24: twenty-fifth batch -- Elephant Bush (deliberately checked against Jade Plant, already in this catalog, for genus-content bleed; none found -- different families, Didiereaceae vs. Crassulaceae), a fern cluster (Bird's Nest Fern, Rabbit's Foot Fern -- resolved to the full varietal name Davallia solida var. fejeensis, Autumn Fern), and three toxic caudiciform/succulent species (Firestick, Desert Rose, Madagascar Palm), plus Umbrella Plant. Elephant Bush is notable for a fully honest single-source record: only RHS was found to carry a dedicated page for this species across all ten admissible domains (confirmed by direct URL probing of the other nine), so every field is attributed to RHS alone rather than papering over the gap with a weaker source. Corrected a chill-damage/freeze-survival conflation on Desert Rose using this catalog's own established Oleander precedent (b19): the record had set chill_damage_f=32 from UF/IFAS's 'Freeze tolerant (below 32°F): No... DO NOT let them freeze' language, but that is a survival threshold, not a damage-onset figure -- the same UF/IFAS page's own two-tier distinction gives 'Chill tolerant (55°F-35°F): Yes, but leaf yellowing and leaf drop may occur' as the actual damage-onset figure, corroborated by this catalog's existing convention of recording the higher onset temperature for comparable tropical/succulent species (Crown of Thorns 35, Amaryllis 35). Corrected to 35 using the same citation, re-quoted to the correct tier. Bird's Nest Fern got three repairs: night_f_min was corrected from 50°F (Clemson's threshold for returning an outdoor-summered plant indoors) to 55°F (Missouri Botanical Garden's actual stated indoor nighttime floor, from the same source already used for this record's paired day_f_min/day_f_max); outdoor_sun_exposure was narrowed from ['part_shade', 'full_shade'] to just ['part_shade'] after two structured, species-specific sources (NC State, RHS) both stopped short of a full-shade tag while only one looser range statement (MOBOT) extended to it; and soil_drainage and soil_ph_max were both left null on genuine cross-source disagreements -- soil_drainage because three already-cited sources (NC State's paired Good-Drainage-and-Moist tags, RHS's 'moist but well-drained' field plus grit-amended compost, and Clemson's explicit root-rot warning against a wet saucer) described wanting moisture AND drainage together, which doesn't cleanly map to moisture_retentive alone; soil_ph_max because NC State's Acid-only tag (ceiling 6.0) directly conflicts with RHS's 'Acid or Neutral' field, which implies a materially higher ceiling. Umbrella Plant's soil_ph_max was similarly nulled after RHS's explicit 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral' tolerance (affirmatively including Alkaline) contradicted NC State's Neutral-topped ceiling of 8.0, paralleling how this record had already left soil_ph_min null for the same kind of missing bound. toxic_to_pets confirmed clean and properly scoped across all four non-null verdicts: Bird's Nest Fern and Rabbit's Foot Fern both false (Clemson's dedicated pet-safety sections, one naming dogs and cats explicitly, the other a direct ferns-are-non-toxic-to-pets determination); Firestick and Desert Rose both true via explicit NC State 'Problem for Cats'/'Problem for Dogs' tags, Desert Rose further corroborated by RHS naming both dogs and cats.
